messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PAGER fired for service=rate-limiter-eu (high error rate) -- escalation policy: SRE Primary
incident-bot: summary: sudden surge of 429/500s from limiter-frontend, many tenants seeing unexpected throttles, automated detection flagged quota-mapper anomalies
pagerduty-bot: Incident: PD123456 - Rate limiter anomaly (auto-page) — triggered 3512346789
sre-oncall: acked — taking it. oncall ETA 2m. I'm looking at dashboards now :eyes:
sre-oncall: quick check: is this a capacity spike or a config change?
kai-chen: I saw a deploy 6m ago to quota-mapper v2-beta. @sre-oncall can you confirm if v2 is live in eu-west-1?
sre-oncall: checking deploy history... `/deploys --service quota-mapper --region eu-west-1 --last 10m`
sre-oncall: output: 1 deploy by @eng-runtime at +00:06, image: quota-mapper:v2-beta
maya: hmm that matches timeline. We have early-stage rollout rule that should be opt-in per-tenant — looks like a tag mismatch may have applied globally
infra-ops: I'm pulling logs from limiter-frontend: `kubectl logs -l app=limiter-frontend -n prod --tail 200` — seeing lots of `ERR quota_resolve: missing-tag -> apply default-zero`
nicole: customer-impact: CS reports two customers in eu-west seeing production 429s for embeddings and text-gen. No major revenue customers hit yet, but several SMBs complaining.
eng-runtime: attaching trace snippet from trace sampling (redacted):
```
2023-11-09T13:12:34Z limiter-frontend request_id=abcd1234 tenant_id=acct-9876 quota_tag=none -> applied_quota=0 latency=12ms code=429
2023-11-09T13:12:35Z quota-mapper resolve tenant_id=acct-9876 tags=[] matched_rule=none fallback=global-zero
```

sre-oncall: that points to quota-mapper falling back to global-zero for tenants without a tag. sudden fallback -> mass throttles. Did the new deploy change tag resolution semantics?
kai-chen: v2-beta changed precedence: it treats unknown tags as explicit `null` rather than inherit. There's a feature flag that should have been off in eu-west; looks like infra flag wasn't set.
maya: ok mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag off to restore previous behavior 2) rollback quota-mapper to previous version 3) temporarily increase global default quota to reduce 429s 4) add flow-level bypass for critical customers
icer: (reaction) :thumbsup: to quick list
sre-oncall: immediate plan: flip feature flag + bump global default for 10m, watch errors. Who can flip the flag?
infra-ops: I can flip it in org-ops console. Confirming path: `orgops.flags.set quota-mapper.v2.tag-fallback eu-west-1 false`
nicole: if we flip flag first, CS wants message template for affected customers. ETA on mitigation?
infra-ops: doing the flag flip now —
incident-bot: audit: flag change requested by infra-ops at 3512346835
infra-ops: done. response: propagated to all quota-mapper pods in eu-west in ~18s
sre-oncall: monitoring... error rate dropping, still some 429s but down 75%
eng-runtime: while we watch, I'll prepare a safe rollback in case flag flip doesn't stabilize. rollback plan: `/deploy rollback quota-mapper --to=stable-1.14 --region=eu-west-1`
kai-chen: good. Also we should run a targeted cache flush for quota-mapper prefixes — some pods may have cached the null tag. Command: `kubectl exec -it -l app=quota-mapper -n prod -- /bin/quota-tool flush --prefix=tags`
maya: CS update draft: "We're aware of an incident causing increased throttling for some customers in EU-West. We've applied a configuration change and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a postmortem if there's continued impact." — anyone want to tweak?
nicole: add estimated start time: ~13:07 UTC and affected operations: embeddings, text generation. Ask customers to retry after 1 minute.
sre-oncall: errors down to baseline. I'm keeping the page open for 10 more mins and will watch for regression.
eng-runtime: rolling verification checks: synthetic traffic shows stable token throughput. No steady-state 500s.
infra-ops: starting cache flush on quota-mapper pods now to remove stale state; running as background job (no restart).
incident-bot: PD update: note added to PD123456 by infra-ops: feature flag flipped; cache flush initiated
kai-chen: root cause hypothesis: v2-beta changed unknown-tag behaviour + feature-flag misconfig = global fallback to zero quota. Secondary cause: some tenants lacked tag metadata, exposing the behavior immediately.
nicole: CS will proactively message impacted customers who opened tickets, internal blameless note ready.
sre-oncall: OK I'm clearing on-call page: leaving monitoring hand to @kai-chen for 30m post-mitigation, then close. If we see re-escalation, PD escalate to SRE Secondary.
kai-chen: ack — will monitor. Can we add an alert to catch unexpected tag-fallback at the feature-flag level? i.e., alert if >5% tenants map to default-zero within 5m.
eng-runtime: good idea, I can add a short-term alert and a long-term eval to ensure rollouts have a safety gate. PR incoming: #4721
maya: thank you all — will capture timeline for postmortem. Quick note for timeline: deploy -> 13:06, PD page -> 13:12, flag flip -> 13:13, errors normalized -> 13:17.
sre-oncall: closing thread to note handoff: monitoring with kai-chen; reopen if any regression. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: PD123456 status: acknowledged and mitigation applied — awaiting close
